gates.gate: secret-shaped strings in diff (grep over git diff origin/main...HEAD)
gates.notes: Patterns: postgres URLs, Bearer, ghp_, sk-, AKIA, ntn_, JWT, private-key blocks, neon.tech, supabase.co, quoted passwords. Only matches were unrelated words in artifacts/metrics/debt-ledger.yaml prose. No secrets or real-looking hosts in code, tests, docs.
No AI attribution trailers, no secret-shaped strings.

update and resetToDefaults both call assertAvailabilityAdmin (isAvailabilityAdminRole against AVAILABILITY_ADMIN_ROLES) before any DB access; get is read-only for any tenant user and exposes canEdit. Tests assert FORBIDDEN for USER with no writes.

tenantId comes from ctx.tenant (router) or ctx.user.tenantId (appointments) and is passed explicitly in every where/data in router, loader, count and findMany. Input schema has no tenantId; smuggled tenantId test present; expectEveryCallTenantScoped used in router and enforcement tests. Settings upsert/updateMany, deleteMany, createMany all keyed on tenantId. Save/reset run in one $transaction.

Both new tables: RLS enabled, policy with USING and WITH CHECK on tenantId = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true); FK to tenants ON DELETE CASCADE; CHECKs on weekday, minute bounds, range order, date order, reason non-blank; unique indexes; cap CHECK 1..500. Additive only. FORCE RLS not set, consistent with the case_types shape it copies; the app-level tenantId filter remains the primary boundary.

Strict ints with bounds, exactly 7 unique weekdays, max 6 ranges per day, overlap rejection, max 200 closures, closure span <= 366 days, dates 2000..2100 and calendar-valid, reason trimmed and max 200, timezone validated then canonicalised, buffers 0..240, cap 1..500. Bounds mirrored in DB CHECKs.

No raw SQL in calendar module production code. tests/integration/availability.test.ts uses positional parameters for all values; remaining interpolations are constant literals (LIKE prefix, SET LOCAL TIME ZONE constant, static bootstrap statements).

Booking errors state weekday, configured hour ranges, timezone, the requested date. Closure reasons are never included (CLOSED_DATE message is 'The firm is closed on <date>'). Conflict and forbidden messages are generic. Missing-migration path logs only the Prisma code.

Update payload bounded (<= 42 ranges, <= 200 closures). findNextSlot: maxDaysAhead <= 365, candidates capped at 2000, cap read is one bounded findMany, <= 5 queries. durationMinutes has no upper bound but is a pre-existing schema and candidate generation is capped.

Diff only removes the legacy hour helpers (moved verbatim into availability-enforcement.ts) and swaps in assertAppointmentWithinAvailability / loadTenantAvailability / findNextSlotWithinAvailability in create, reschedule and findNextSlot. No ownership-check lines changed. forceOverrideConflicts does not bypass availability.
Skipped per lead instruction (test slot held by code-review job). Replaced by the diff grep above.
Skipped per lead instruction. Low relevance: no dependency changes in this diff.

findings.issue: Daily cap is count-then-insert, not atomic: concurrent bookings can exceed the cap slightly. A business-limit overrun, not a confidentiality, tenancy or privilege issue; an authenticated user can only affect their own tenant. Three Codex HIGH findings are waived for it.
findings.fix: Waiver is acceptable from a security standpoint (accepted in ADR-081, tracked in gh #913 and debt ledger PG-202-AVAILABILITY-KNOWN-LIMITS-001). Locked fix later: per-tenant pg_advisory_xact_lock around count and insert. The waiver author is still 'pending owner confirmation'; the owner should confirm before merge.

findings.issue: appointment_settings RLS has USING but no WITH CHECK (finding T2, gh #910). Not introduced by PG-202, but PG-202 writes two new columns on that table. App-level tenantId scoping covers it.
findings.fix: Tracked as gh #910 / PG-202-APPOINTMENT-SETTINGS-RLS-WITH-CHECK-001; add WITH CHECK in a separate migration.

findings.issue: findNextSlot input (pre-existing): attendeeId is an unbounded string and durationMinutes has no maximum. Candidate count is capped at 2000, so work is bounded. Not tracked anywhere.
findings.fix: Optional hardening in a later change: z.string().max(64) and durationMinutes max 1440.

limitations: Review is manual plus grep only. Per lead constraints I did not run gitleaks, pnpm audit, snyk, semgrep or trivy, and did not run tests; the cross-tenant and FORBIDDEN tests were confirmed present by reading, not execution. The STOA-spec SAST and dependency gates therefore produced no result; this PASS covers code review, the diff secret grep and the dependency-change check only. I did not open the validation-matrix logs, sql-review.json or the integration test run output. If the strict STOA rule (any finding, any severity, is FAIL unless formally accepted) applies, the first two LOW findings are accepted/tracked (ADR-081, gh #913, gh #910) and the third is new and untracked, so the lead may want to track it or accept it.
